name: Theoricapades
domain: Pure & Theoretical Mathematics — what math is, what makes it true, and how you live as a mathematician

categories.name: Foundations & Ontology
categories.about: What mathematics is at bottom, where its structure resides, and whether infinity and mathematical reality are discovered or made.

topics.name: Foundations of Mathematics

hovertip.issue: What is mathematics, at bottom?

poles.label: Platonism
poles.text: Mathematical objects exist independently; we discover them.

poles.label: Formalism
poles.text: Math is symbols and rules; meaning is irrelevant.

poles.label: Intuitionism
poles.text: Math is a construction of the mind; only what can be built is real.

poles.label: Logicism
poles.text: Math reduces to logic; all truths are logical truths.

poles.label: Structuralism
poles.text: Math is about structures and patterns, not objects.

topics.question: What is mathematics, at bottom?
topics.source: BRIEFING_THEORICAPADES_TAXONOMY.md §2, topic 1.1 — Abstracapades 1.1 (the pentad is more complete than Axiomcapades' triad, which drops Logicism and Structuralism).

topics.name: Foundational Bedrock: Sets vs. Categories vs. Types

hovertip.issue: Where does mathematical structure ultimately reside?

poles.label: ZFC Set Theory
poles.text: Classical cumulative hierarchy of sets; the universal standard.

poles.label: Category Theory / Topoi
poles.text: Arrows, functors, universal properties; relations over elements.

poles.label: Homotopy Type Theory (HoTT)
poles.text: Constructive type theory; identity is homotopy equivalence.

topics.question: Where does mathematical structure ultimately reside?
topics.source: BRIEFING_THEORICAPADES_TAXONOMY.md §2, topic 1.2 — Axiomcapades 1.2 (Abstracapades did not cover this).

topics.name: The Law of Excluded Middle: Classical vs. Constructive Logic

hovertip.issue: Is proof by contradiction genuine knowledge?

poles.label: Classical Logic
poles.text: LEM holds; proof by contradiction is fully valid.

poles.label: Constructive Logic
poles.text: LEM rejected; existence requires an explicit witness.

topics.question: Is proof by contradiction genuine knowledge?
topics.source: BRIEFING_THEORICAPADES_TAXONOMY.md §2, topic 1.3 — Axiomcapades 1.3 (the LEM detail; Abstracapades 2.1 is the same topic in plainer form).

topics.name: Discovered vs Invented

hovertip.issue: Is math discovered or invented?

poles.label: Discovered
poles.text: Math is out there; we find it.

poles.label: Invented
poles.text: Math is made up by humans.

topics.question: Is math discovered or invented?

topics.name: Mathematical Universe Hypothesis: Realist Ontology

hovertip.issue: Is reality made of mathematics, or is mathematics made by human minds?

poles.label: Radical Mathematical Realism
poles.text: Our universe literally is a mathematical structure.

poles.label: Epistemic Anti-Realism
poles.text: Mathematics is a human cognitive language and mapping tool.

topics.question: Is reality made of mathematics, or is mathematics made by human minds?

topics.name: Infinity: Actual vs Potential

hovertip.issue: Is infinity a thing, or just a direction?

poles.label: Actual infinity
poles.text: A completed thing (Cantor).

poles.label: Potential infinity
poles.text: A process, never finished (Aristotle).

topics.question: Is infinity a thing, or just a direction?

categories.name: Method & Style
categories.about: How mathematicians attack problems, how abstract they go, and whether they think in pictures or symbols.

topics.name: The Rising Sea vs. The Hammer & Chisel

hovertip.issue: Do you submerge problems in abstract machinery or crack them with direct ingenuity?

poles.label: The Rising Sea
poles.text: Build vast conceptual machinery until the theorem becomes obvious.

poles.label: The Hammer & Chisel
poles.text: Direct assault: hard combinatorics, brutal inequalities, ad-hoc ingenuity.

topics.question: Do you submerge problems in abstract machinery or crack them with direct ingenuity?

topics.name: Abstraction: Deep Generalization vs. Concrete Jewels

hovertip.issue: Are you captivated by universal abstractions or exceptional concrete gems?

poles.label: Extreme Structural Abstraction
poles.text: Infinity-categories, motives, universal properties; the meta-pattern.

poles.label: Exceptional Concrete Jewels
poles.text: The Monster group, the Leech lattice, E8; unique idiosyncratic structures.

topics.question: Are you captivated by universal abstractions or exceptional concrete gems?

topics.name: Abstraction: High vs Low

hovertip.issue: How abstract should math be?

poles.label: High abstraction
poles.text: Category theory, the general.

poles.label: Low abstraction
poles.text: Concrete computation, the particular.

topics.question: How abstract should math be?

topics.name: Erdős's "The Book": Proof Aesthetics

hovertip.issue: What is the highest form of mathematical beauty in a proof?

poles.label: Luminous Simplicity ("The Book")
poles.text: Two lines of breathtaking, unexpected ingenuity.

poles.label: Architectural Monumentality
poles.text: A 1,000-page cathedral of structural logic.

poles.label: Constructive Computational Revelation
poles.text: An illuminating algorithm that calculates the inner mechanics.

topics.question: What is the highest form of mathematical beauty in a proof?

topics.name: Visual vs Symbolic

hovertip.issue: Do you think in pictures or in symbols?

poles.label: Visual
poles.text: Pictures, diagrams, geometry.

poles.label: Symbolic
poles.text: Formulas, algebra, symbols.

topics.question: Do you think in pictures or in symbols?

topics.name: Intuition: Trust vs Distrust

hovertip.issue: Do you trust mathematical intuition?

poles.label: Trust
poles.text: Intuition guides you right.

poles.label: Distrust
poles.text: Intuition misleads; only proof counts.

topics.question: Do you trust mathematical intuition?

categories.name: Branches & Territory
categories.about: Which branch of pure mathematics is home, and where you stand on the pure/applied divide.

topics.name: The Quadrivium of Pure Mathematics

hovertip.issue: Where does your primary mathematical heart dwell?

poles.label: Algebra & Symmetry
poles.text: Groups, rings, fields, Galois theory; symmetry and transformation.

poles.label: Geometry & Topology
poles.text: Manifolds, knot theory, shape and invariants under deformation.

poles.label: Analysis & Continua
poles.text: Limits, measures, continuous variation; real and complex analysis.

poles.label: Number Theory & Arithmetic
poles.text: Primes, modular forms, elliptic curves; the Queen of Mathematics.

topics.question: Where does your primary mathematical heart dwell?
topics.source: BRIEFING_THEORICAPADES_TAXONOMY.md §2, topic 3.1 — Axiomcapades 3.1 (the tetrad adds Number Theory, which Abstracapades' triad omitted).

topics.name: Combinatorics & Discrete Structures

hovertip.issue: How strong is your passion for the finite and discrete?

poles.label: Affinity
poles.text: Graphs, posets, extremal combinatorics, partition theory (rate 0–100).

topics.question: How strong is your passion for the finite and discrete?

topics.name: Discrete vs Continuous

hovertip.issue: Do you live in the discrete world or the continuous one?

poles.label: Discrete
poles.text: Combinatorics, number theory, graphs.

poles.label: Continuous
poles.text: Analysis, topology, geometry.

topics.question: Do you live in the discrete world or the continuous one?

topics.name: Pure vs Applied

hovertip.issue: The skin-defining divide — where do you stand?

poles.label: Pure
poles.text: Math for its own sake.

poles.label: Applied
poles.text: Math for what it does.

topics.question: The skin-defining divide — where do you stand?

categories.name: Proof & Verification
categories.about: What counts as a proof — computer-checked, human-consented, or rigorously closed.

topics.name: Computer Proof

hovertip.issue: Is the Four Color Theorem proved?

poles.label: Accept
poles.text: A computer-assisted proof is a real proof.

poles.label: Reject
poles.text: If a human can't check it, it isn't a proof.

topics.question: Is the Four Color Theorem proved?

topics.name: Proof Verification: Computer Proof Assistants vs. Human Social Consensus

hovertip.issue: Does absolute certainty require interactive proof assistants?

poles.label: Machine-Checked Formalization
poles.text: Lean, Coq, Isabelle; verified to the kernel.

poles.label: Human Social Consensus
poles.text: Math is a dialogue among human minds; machine proofs miss comprehension.

topics.question: Does absolute certainty require interactive proof assistants?

topics.name: Axiom of Choice (AC) Stance

hovertip.issue: How do you relate to the Axiom of Choice?

poles.label: Unconditional Acceptance (ZFC)
poles.text: Indispensable; without AC, functional analysis collapses.

poles.label: Skeptical Restriction (ZF + Dependent Choice)
poles.text: Accept weak choice; reject non-measurable sets.

poles.label: Defiant Rejection (ZF + AD)
poles.text: Every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable.

topics.question: How do you relate to the Axiom of Choice?

topics.name: Conjecture Orientation: Conjecture-Solver vs. Theory-Builder

hovertip.issue: Do you slay famous open problems or build new mathematical worlds?

poles.label: Conjecture Solver
poles.text: Hunts white whales: Riemann, BSD, Goldbach.

poles.label: Theory Builder
poles.text: Develops new conceptual languages where old problems dissolve.

topics.question: Do you slay famous open problems or build new mathematical worlds?

topics.name: Rigor vs Intuition

hovertip.issue: Do you trust formal rigor, or mathematical intuition?

poles.label: Rigor
poles.text: Formal proof, no gaps.

poles.label: Intuition
poles.text: Insight, the feel of it.

topics.question: Do you trust formal rigor, or mathematical intuition?

categories.name: Beauty & Reality
categories.about: What makes mathematics beautiful, and how pure mathematics relates to physical reality.

topics.name: Elegance vs Power

hovertip.issue: What makes good math — a beautiful proof, or a powerful theorem?

poles.label: Elegance
poles.text: A beautiful proof.

poles.label: Power
poles.text: A powerful result.

topics.question: What makes good math — a beautiful proof, or a powerful theorem?

topics.name: Simplicity vs Depth

hovertip.issue: Do you value simple results or deep ones?

poles.label: Simplicity
poles.text: Clean, spare results.

poles.label: Depth
poles.text: Rich, complex structures.

topics.question: Do you value simple results or deep ones?

topics.name: Beauty: Essential vs Incidental

hovertip.issue: Is beauty in math a guide to truth, or just a pleasure?

poles.label: Essential
poles.text: Beauty is a sign of truth.

poles.label: Incidental
poles.text: Beauty is a nice bonus.

topics.question: Is beauty in math a guide to truth, or just a pleasure?

topics.name: G.H. Hardy's Stance: Proud Inutility vs. Unreasonable Effectiveness

hovertip.issue: Is pure math untainted because it has no application, or miraculous because it secretly mirrors physics?

poles.label: Proud Inutility
poles.text: Pure math is noble precisely because it has no base applications.

poles.label: Unreasonable Effectiveness
poles.text: Esoteric pure math mysteriously anticipates the laws of nature.

topics.question: Is pure math untainted because it has no application, or miraculous because it secretly mirrors physics?

topics.name: Pure Mathematics vs. Physics Boundary

hovertip.issue: Should pure math be guided by internal consistency or physical insight?

poles.label: Autonomous Self-Reference
poles.text: Math answers only to its own internal logic.

poles.label: Physical Symbiosis
poles.text: Breakthroughs are fertilized by quantum field theory and relativity.

topics.question: Should pure math be guided by internal consistency or physical insight?

categories.name: The Mathematical Life
categories.about: How you live as a mathematician — alone or together, chalk or computer, teaching or research.

topics.name: The Social Mode: The Wandering Erdős vs. The Monastic Perelman

hovertip.issue: How do you pursue the mathematical life?

poles.label: Hyper-Collaborative / Itinerant (Erdős)
poles.text: Hundreds of coauthors, constant dialogue, math in coffee houses.

poles.label: Ascetic Monastic Solitude (Perelman)
poles.text: Years alone, zero distractions, indifferent to prizes.

topics.question: How do you pursue the mathematical life?
topics.source: BRIEFING_THEORICAPADES_TAXONOMY.md §2, topic 6.1 — Axiomcapades 6.1 (the vivid Erdős/Perelman framing of Abstracapades 6.1's Collaboration vs Solitude).

topics.name: The Instrument: Chalk & Slate vs. Digital Computation

hovertip.issue: How do you explore mathematics?

poles.label: Traditional Chalkboard
poles.text: Dust on slate, live seminars, pure mental calculation.

poles.label: Digital & Computational
poles.text: Sage, Mathematica, experimental math, algorithmic visualization.

topics.question: How do you explore mathematics?

topics.name: The Reward: Aesthetic Epiphany vs. Institutional Immortality

hovertip.issue: What is the ultimate reward of pure mathematics?

poles.label: Private Aesthetic Epiphany
poles.text: The silent ecstasy of understanding an eternal truth.

poles.label: Institutional Immortality
poles.text: Fields Medal, Abel Prize, named theorems, legacy in the literature.

topics.question: What is the ultimate reward of pure mathematics?

topics.name: Publication vs Perfection

hovertip.issue: Do you publish fast, or perfect first?

poles.label: Publish quickly
poles.text: Get it out.

poles.label: Polish forever
poles.text: Perfect it first.

topics.question: Do you publish fast, or perfect first?

topics.name: Teaching vs Research

hovertip.issue: Do you value teaching or research more?

poles.label: Teaching
poles.text: Passing it on.

poles.label: Research
poles.text: Pushing it forward.

topics.question: Do you value teaching or research more?
